Bank draft to me means money order or cashiers check - Both are hard to place stop payments on because they're supposed to be treated "like cash" and can be cashed at any bank, not just the one that issued it.

So for example, Bank A made the bank draft, then puts a stop payment on it, meanwhile someone brings it to Bank B, which has no idea Bank A placed a stop payment until a few days later.

Bank B would almost certainly not have the cash to give, and would put a hold on the majority of the funds until it fully cleared, but they could be out some of the money they made available to the check casher before they knew there was a stop payment. Which is probably why Bank A didn't immediately just cancel it.

The smarter decision would be to never use that method for that amount of money, and I have a feeling the bank wasn't actually the one that recommended it.
The fact that banks are still using this archaic system is the problem, and entirely the bank's fault.
